subject: An atlas of echoes: five charts stacked in depth from the first reflections to the late tail, each plotting its echoes as stars by magnitude, lit from the west door's source star.
controls: nave: position; the charts recede further apart, the back chart travelling about 60 px up and to the right, so a long nave is a deep stack.
stone: scale; star magnitudes fall from chart to chart, steeply on soft stone (back charts nearly empty) and hardly at all on hard stone.
choir: count; each chart plots 4 bright stars at 0 (discrete echoes) up to 26 fainter ones at 100 (a diffuse wash).
doors: position; the whole stack moves away from the source star along a dashed trail, 18 to 98 px.
risks: The stack reads as cards or windows before it reads as time; the 'first' and 'V' labels carry a lot.
Stars on back charts only show in the thin uncovered strip, so stone's change lives mostly in that strip and in small dots (lint warns on dots under 3 px).
Choir changes count and star size together; star size is stone's channel too, so the two blur on the front chart.
Star atlas is a borrowed language for a building; nothing says 'stone nave' except the source labelled 'door'.
